tagline: Navigate relationships in DAX to fetch values and tables from related sides

slides.title: Two Functions, Two Directions
slides.body: RELATED() and RELATEDTABLE() both traverse relationships — but in opposite directions. RELATED() moves from the MANY side to the ONE side, returning a single scalar value. RELATEDTABLE() moves from the ONE side to the MANY side, returning a full table of matching rows.
slides.keyPoint: RELATED = many → one (returns a scalar). RELATEDTABLE = one → many (returns a table). Both require an active relationship and an active row context.

slides.title: FactSales — The 'Many' Side
slides.caption: Multiple sale rows can share the same ProductID

slides.title: RELATED() — Add Category to FactSales
slides.caption: Calculated column on FactSales pulls data from DimProduct
slides.explanation: This calculated column is evaluated row-by-row on FactSales. For each row, RELATED() follows the active relationship from the current ProductID to DimProduct and returns the matching Category value. This works because we are on the MANY side navigating to the ONE side.

slides.title: Result — RELATED() Adds Category to Each Sale
slides.caption: Each sale row now shows its product category from DimProduct

slides.title: RELATEDTABLE() — Count Sales per Product
slides.caption: Calculated column on DimProduct uses the ONE → MANY direction
slides.explanation: These calculated columns are evaluated row-by-row on DimProduct. For each product row, RELATEDTABLE() returns the full table of matching FactSales rows — allowing COUNTROWS, SUMX, MINX, or any table function to aggregate them.

slides.title: Result — RELATEDTABLE() Aggregates per Product
slides.caption: Each product row now has its sales count and total revenue

slides.title: PL-300 Exam Traps
bullets: RELATED() requires row context — it CANNOT be used directly in a measure without an iterator (SUMX, FILTER, AVERAGEX) that creates row context row by row.
RELATED() only traverses from many to one — using it from the one side causes an error. Use RELATEDTABLE() instead.
Both functions need an ACTIVE relationship. For inactive relationships (e.g., role-playing dimensions), use USERELATIONSHIP() inside CALCULATE.
RELATEDTABLE() can be used inside SUMX in a measure: SUMX(RELATEDTABLE(FactSales), FactSales[Revenue]) — this creates the row context needed.
Calculated columns using RELATED() increase model size because the column values are physically stored in VertiPaq. Prefer measures using RELATED() inside iterators when possible.
